opening_message:

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E043.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Karen Sloan (E043) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin is permitted under policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E043 is a contractor with basic training, contradicting HR's note of full-time. Contractors max out at read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes for E043 conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin), while the Security DB states contractor with basic training (which caps access at read and never permits admin). Given the conflicting evidence and that admin is strictly prohibited for contractors, I apply the more restrictive, policy-safe interpretation and grant the maximum level permitted under that interpretation: read. I do not grant above the verified maximum.
